links.outcome: Standalone AI fracture sensitivity versus radiographer baseline sensitivity
links.effect: Standalone AI sensitivity 75.6% (46.2% for subtle fractures) versus radiographer baseline sensitivity 91.6%
links.quote: Standalone AI sensitivity was 75.6%, falling to 46.2% for subtle fractures, below the radiographers’ baseline sensitivity of 91.6%.

links.outcome: Errors introduced versus corrected by radiographers after viewing AI output
links.effect: Radiographers corrected 11 errors and introduced 1 with AI assistance (net gain 10); changed decision in only 11 of 729 discordant cases
links.quote: With AI assistance, radiographers corrected 11 errors and introduced 1, a net gain of 10 cases.

links.outcome: Operational reliability: examinations with no or incomplete AI output
links.effect: No or incomplete AI output for 8.8% of acquired examinations
links.quote: No or incomplete AI output was returned for 8.8% of acquired examinations.

openai.sample_unit: musculoskeletal examinations with paired radiographer reads

links.outcome: Radiographer diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Accuracy increased from 97.6% to 98.0% with AI assistance (exact McNemar p = 0.0064); radiographers corrected 11 errors and introduced 1, a net gain of 10 cases.
links.quote: Radiographers’ baseline accuracy was high (97.6%; specificity 99.0%) and improved modestly with AI assistance (98.0%; exact McNemar p = 0.0064).

links.outcome: Fractures missed by standalone AI, including subtle fractures
links.effect: Standalone AI sensitivity was 75.6%, falling to 46.2% for subtle fractures, versus radiographers’ baseline sensitivity of 91.6%.
links.quote: Standalone AI sensitivity was 75.6%, falling to 46.2% for subtle fractures, below the radiographers’ baseline sensitivity of 91.6%.

links.outcome: Nonadoption of correct AI recommendations in discordant cases
links.effect: Radiographers changed decisions in only 11 of 729 discordant cases; most negative interactions involved correct AI recommendations not adopted.
links.quote: Radiographers changed their decision in only 11 of 729 discordant cases, and most negative interactions were correct AI recommendations not adopted.

links.effect: Radiographers' baseline accuracy was 97.6% and improved to 98.0% with AI assistance.
links.quote: Radiographers’ baseline accuracy was high (97.6%; specificity 99.0%) and improved modestly with AI assistance (98.0%; exact McNemar p = 0.0064).

links.effect: While standalone AI sensitivity was lower than baseline human performance, combined performance benefited from complementary algorithmic performance.
links.quote: AI assistance delivered a small, selective benefit arising from complementary rather than superior algorithmic performance.

links.effect: Radiographers changed their decision in only 11 of 729 discordant cases, often failing to adopt correct AI recommendations.
